opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Black (employee ID E008) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E008.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Black (E008) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, maximum is write unless her role owns the system; Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not permitted. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security record for Karen Black (E008): contractor with basic security training. Contractors cannot be granted admin, and write requires advanced training, so maximum level is read. Requested admin to Source Code; recommend granting read.
reason: Karen Black (E008) requested admin to Source Code. The team notes conflict on employment type: HR says full-time (max write, but admin not allowed since Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code), while Security says contractor with basic security training (max read; admin never allowed for contractors, write requires advanced training). Admin is not permitted under either interpretation. Given the conflicting records, I grant the safe ceiling that does not violate policy in any scenario: read.
